Question
========

A simple interest loan for \$`r P` is taken out at `r sr` annual percentage rate. A partial payment of \$`r payment` is made `r days` days into the loan period. After this payment, what will the remaining balance of the loan be?

(Assume 365 days per year.)


Solution
========

First, calculate the interest accrued during the `r days` days.

$$I=`r P`\cdot `r r/100` \cdot \frac{`r days`}{365}$$

$$I=`r I`$$

To find the remaining balance, add the interest to the principal and subtract the payment.

$$`r P`+`r I`-`r payment`=`r P+I-payment`$$

You can round to the nearest penny to get the current balance is `r sprintf("%.2f",ans)` USD.
